notes.title: LaserZone is now released on Steam!
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings[/h1]

Hello, everyone! 
I am Jung Hwan Hwang – the level designer behind LaserZone. 
I’m speaking on behalf of our team and our director since I am the only person who can write in English.

[h1]What We've Been Up to[/h1]

As you guessed, LaserZone has been finally released! Our team is excited and extremely happy at the moment.
It took more than 3 years to release our game, and there had been tough problems lurking around the corners. The first two years were slow-going since we lacked manpower. In addition, there were conflicts between crew members, COVID-19 prevented offline meetings, and our rating got rejected once. A handful of reasons delayed the release, and it hit our team’s morale even though no one said anything about it.

However, our director aims to complete any product no matter what. His tenacity gave us the motivation to stay cool and deliver a polished game to the market.
7 months have passed since the initial release date. However, having tested our game 7 months before and now, I’m glad we didn’t rush our release.

[h1]Q&A[/h1]

In the last news, we promised you to give extra information about the game on the release date. 
We would like to clear out some of the questions you got by preparing a Q&A. I wrote down 4 answers for 4 corresponding questions.
This section excludes any information that is already on the Store Page.
 
Q. How much content is in the game? How long is the playtime?

A. There are a total of [u]160 maps[/u] available, split into 6 Chapters.
132 maps are designed to deliver the puzzle-solving experience. 39 maps out of the 132 serve as tutorials. They teach you how to use, exploit, and combine newly introduced game mechanics.
On the other hand, you can take a rest in the other 28 maps. They offer free resources for upgrades and often include cinematic events for advancing the story. 
Based on the FGT reports we’ve collected, it will approximately take [u]7~9 hours[/u] to finish the game. But please note that playtime may vary between players.

Q. How difficult is the game?

A. Our game targets [u]casual-to-mid core[/u] players.
Based on a scale of 1 to 10, the average difficulty for Chapters starts at 2, and gradually increases up to 6. 
However, there are some difficulty spikes to keep good players interested. Some maps require faster reflexes than others too.
But after you overcome them, difficulty settles down for a short time.
You can easily complete Chapters 1 and 2, but you will need to start paying some attention from there.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/8f4a94a3322b505027cd3055a9a896e4429e54ac.jpg[/img]


Q. Please tell us about Configuration options.

A. LaserZone supports resolution options up to 2560x1440(QHD) and custom key-bindings. Controller support is NOT in the game. Texture options are NOT provided because the game does not require high-end PCs, and CPU is more important than GPU (for playing this game). 

Q. Will there be any future support from the development team?
A. We are planning to add [u]Steam Achievements[/u]. We will attempt to [u]fix any unexpected bugs[/u] by receiving reports from players on the Steam Forum too.
But please note that the official release version for LaserZone is meant to be [u]a complete experience, a finished product[/u]. 
While we don’t have any concrete plans at the moment, we will consider adding new features and content if a suggestion receives a certain degree of popularity.

[h1]Signing Off[/h1]

I hope that answers your questions!
Again, thank you very much for checking out LaserZone! 
And if you decided to get the game, we hope you enjoy it!

notes.title: LaserZone is coming to Steam soon!
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings[/h1]

Hello, everyone! I am Jung Hwan Hwang – the level designer behind LaserZone. 
I hope you are staying safe and strong in this global pandemic.
I’m speaking on behalf of our team and our director since I am the only person who can write in English.

[h1]What We've Been Up to[/h1]

As you guessed, LaserZone is going to be released soon!
For some, it must have been a very long waiting, especially if you happened to come across the game at Busan Indie Connect Festival (an annual indie-game show held in South Korea), or started following the game in 2020.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/8e62027b2736e276df2255854c1e1cf95c782a30.png[/img]
[i]Our game, listed with other 149 indie games in BIC Festival.[/i]

We also acknowledge that 2 months have passed since Dev Log #3, which might have left some people wondering what is going on with the development. So please, let me explain what occurred during the last 2 months. 
If not interested, you can skip below!

There are three reasons why the release got pushed back from June again :
[olist]
[*] After the 2nd Focus Group Test (or FGT), we took our time to improve the game and gather testers for the final FGT. It cost us 1 week.
[*] Then, we started working on a new trailer which needed 2 weeks. We managed to get it done in June and thought we were ready for release.
[*] However, by the time our trailer was ready, the Game Rating and Administration Committee had just begun rating LaserZone. 
[/olist]
Meeting qualifications for a rating request, and then passing the rating is mandatory in order to release a game in Korea. The entire process took 1 month and is primarily why we had to push back our release.
Back then, we didn’t think the rating process would set us back too much, so that was why I decided not to post any news for the time being. It turned out we were wrong.

The entire team sincerely apologizes for the delay and the lack of communication. However, we also want to thank all users who have waited for us with patience too.

[h1]Signing Off[/h1]

We are planning to [u]release extra information[/u] about the game on release date.
If you are interested in the game, please come again!
We appreciate you for visiting our Store page!

notes.title: Dev Log #3
notes.content:
Hello, everyone. I’m the level designer of the LaserZone. I hope you are having a good day.

It’s been 3 weeks since we posted the announcement about delaying the game’s release. As promised back then, I’m here to relay information about what’s going on in our project before June arrives.


[h1]Game, Ready for Testing[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/5cb8fcd7e9a5332d5e4b3d0cde343e3534663bf8.png[/img]
[i]Our project build folder, including the working .exe file.[/i]

Let’s cut to the chase.
We’ve completed a game version for the upcoming second Focus Group Test (or FGT). 
This version is [b]intended to become the release version[/b] if we don’t receive critical feedback during the second FGT.

That’s basically the gist of this Dev Log. But if you want more details, please continue reading.


[h1]A 3-Week Schedule for Improving the Game[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/489e65882a92302318557fb73c18a81347a4ff3e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/0441ca66a5c3111d4b418ad94c0d3d7224cdc38f.png[/img]
[i]We’ve been using a new project-management program called “Monday”.[/i]

After the first FGT, these are the four main goals we’ve been attempting to accomplish:

[b][olist]
[*] Reducing action/control difficulty in Chapter 4~6
[*] Getting rid of as many bugs as possible
[*] Improving controllability for UI and in-game actions
[*] Implementing a feature that teaches new mechanics for players
[/olist][/b]

We also wanted to address relatively less-urgent tasks such as improving animations, refining English translations, and sound design within the milestone.

Monday tells us our completion rate for the latest version is at [b]95.9%[/b]. 94 out of 98 tasks have been done, and the rest is something that we couldn’t wrap up in time. 
Fortunately, those tasks aren’t critical enough to delay the game’s release (again). We’ll take a look at them after the test is done. 

Right now, we are ready to start the second FGT which will take around 2~3 days. For this FGT, our biggest interest is to receive reports of technical errors that were somehow overlooked during the last 3 weeks of development.

Other members have tested new features, and I did play the game from start to finish. We found and corrected the last critical bug two days ago, so we are expecting the game to fully function.
We’ll also ask our testers if the aforementioned 4 goals have been met.


[h1]Closing[/h1]

If the general consensus from our testers is positive, then we will hire an outsource for a new trailer, and ship the game once we receive the video.

That’s it for today!
I’ll return when we decided what to do after the second FGT.
Thank you for reading, and stay healthy in this global pandemic.

Signing off,
Jung Hwan Hwang

notes.title: Dev Log #2
notes.content:
Greetings, everyone! I’m the level designer of the LaserZone. We hope you are staying healthy in this global pandemic.

I wrote down the very first Dev Log two weeks ago. You might be wondering what has happened since then, so I decided to write another Dev Log to communicate with everyone. Besides, I didn’t want to leave the Newsfeed for too long.

[h2]Boss Fights[/h2]

As mentioned in the previous Log, one of our top priorities is overhauling and improving our Boss-fight experience. Boss-fights from Chapter 3 to 6 felt too challenging because of how frantic they were, and some mechanics were unintuitive and unfair for the player.

Currently, an overhaul for Chapter 3, 4, and 5 has been completed. Our programmer is at hard work implementing the design decisions for Chapter 6. The final Boss-fight is also the most lengthy one, so it’ll take some additional time to finish (but not longer than a week).

Here are some sneak-peek photos from our Boss-fights. Spoiler alert!

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/0f5b63c3e071fc9ffd7cc6c2d103492e88b87d5f.jpg[/img]
[i]I refer to this fight as ‘Spider hell’. By the way, those small things explode.[/i]

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/a2994fa87ddf68b183052b682af5c3ef7fdefdad.jpg[/img]
[i]Curve the bullets, curve the laser.[/i]

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/2ede026dd4dbb17676db9293904355a0b3cdcea6.jpg[/img]
[i]Can you figure out how to solves these puzzles in time?[/i]

[h2]Sound Design[/h2]

Currently, our table(list) for all necessary SFXs is completed. 
As our next step, we’ve contacted an outsource responsible for producing the much-needed sound effects. Based on my expectations, it will approximately take a week or two to finish said work. 

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/76ce8031f859ff860fe6ac6e6435b298cc59148c.png[/img]
[i]Our sound table written in Korean. LaserZone needs 185 new sound files, but this might change in the future.[/i]

[h2]UI Overhaul[/h2]

We are also improving our Main, Pause, Options Menu and In-game UI as we speak. 
We’ve delivered a new framework to another outsource so that we could get additional resources for improved interfaces. They promised our team to return the results in two weeks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/91c8b063c6f8e3cb626dc9eebac10605e3c90a77.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/0f0c06f21ba725bef5a799e73e7b50aecb91f480.png[/img]
[i]Framework for Pause and Options Menu, made by me.[/i]

[h2]English Localization[/h2]

English Localization is 99% complete. I’m responsible for this task, and I only need to translate a few Logs for lore while filling out the missing names for bonus stages.

[h2]Closing[/h2]

That’s it for today.

LaserZone’s release is coming soon. We can’t wait to show the game to our fans and the world!
Thank you for reading, and stay strong.

Signing off,
Jung Hwan Hwang

notes.title: Dev Log #1
notes.content:
Hello, everyone. 

I’m one of the developers behind LaserZone. I’m also responsible for the level design and English translation.

[h1]What We've Been Up to[/h1]

It’s been a long time since we pre-released our game on Steam Store Page in November last year.
I’ve been thinking of writing news for our game, but the last three months gave me little time to spare. And since I’m the only one in the team who speaks English, they are why the news feed was left empty for a long time.

At the time, we were at hard work trying to complete our game within the initial deadline, December 5.
However, our release has been tacitly pushed back because of a few reasons.

First and foremost, I felt that normal maps – which create the bulk of our content – needed a rework. Even though LaserZone embraces action and timing, they were a little too emphasized. I was concerned that some of our puzzle maniacs might not appreciate the delivered content.
Boss fights, sound design, story texts, and a cinematic system for in-game events weren’t ready either.

Meanwhile, COVID-19 wasn’t as critical as we thought since almost everyone in our team (including me) 
worked at home before the pandemic. 
However, offline meetings with 5 people or more have been prohibited by the Government of South Korea. Face-to-face discussions are necessary for clear communication. Attempting to solve everything only with text messengers often resulted in unexpected outcomes, which delayed our release further.

So you might be wondering, ‘how’s the game now?’

In short, it’s [b]100% playable from start to finish[/b]. 
However, we need to polish several aspects of the game. 
Our list of priorities is:
[list]
[*] Decorating maps
[*] Adjusting Boss fights
[*] Adding sound-effects
[*] Reviewing cinematic events
[*] Squashing bugs that plague the gameplay
[*] Optimization
[/list]

[h1]Normal Maps[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/26f9da38e22bc18f01c25bf701e9154bd9df4cbb.png[/img]

For normal maps, we’ve done a significant overhaul. Game-design-wise, they are completed and 100% playable. I believe the new maps will contribute to building the puzzle-game experience we’ve been aiming for.

Currently, our artists are adding lighting-effects to all normal maps, so they look more attractive. We believe beauty to the environment will also stand in contrast to the deadly traps.
And once they finish their work, normal maps won’t undergo any further changes.

[h1]Boss Fights[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/750e7ea3a0272c9c962d8023553e186db22cee5d.png[/img]

Polishing Boss fights is our top priority. 

All Boss fights are currently 100% playable, but whether they are enjoyable or not will always be our question. We are looking into Boss fights in Chapter 3~6, since they are currently too frantic and their surrounding mechanics are difficult to comprehend.
So we are re-designing, adjusting, and playtesting them to deliver the right experience to our players.

[h1]Sound Design[/h1]

Our director and I are in charge of the sound design. We are adding more sound-effects to the game as we speak.

[h1]Cinematic Events[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/c4bc6e39d0f497d97030feb8f42074f81075f6b4.png[/img]

Completing our cinematic events is also our goal.

95% of all necessary texts - both English and Korean - are inserted into the game. Our story writer needs to write additional lines for the ending and extra scenes.
Some animations and visual effects are also not playing in the right place. 
Reviewing our events is a moderate amount of work, so we’ll need at least a month to finish this.

[h1]Bug Fixes and Improvements[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/cf9a92a18fbfb6d530a1c042be17e6a650a6efc0.png[/img]

We are also attempting to get rid of the bugs and add improvements to the game. We’ve been recording and listing bugs on our Trello board. 

[h1]Optimization[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/e93bcd5ab3421db1498a3f24df09c080de5108ad.png[/img]

And finally, optimization. I’ve been tracking maps with low frame-rates and working with our programmer to reduce the symptoms.

Based on what I wrote so far, I’m cautiously expecting our game to be released in March or April. However, this is my expectation, and the others in the team may have a different opinion.

-----

[h1]Closing[/h1]

That’s it for today!
We’ll let you know if something interesting occurs during the end of our development.
Thanks for reading!
